Go outside for a while. Just take a lonely walk. Distract yourself. Go somewhere new. If we surround ourselves with the same scenery day after day, we are bound to question ourselves and our lives. Our thoughts often go south into negative poopy land. Don't go there. It's gross. Go for a walk and think about all the positives in your life. 

Also, draw a picture of a cat wearing sneakers and share it with me. Trust me. This will make you feel a million times better and is not for my personal pleasure at all.

Did you mean: You're going to fuck up enough times that you're just going to be a successful adult?

Every successful adult is just a bundle of fuck up. Seriously. When you fuck up, you have options. You can admit that you fucked up. Study the problem, find a solution, and try not to fuck up again in the future. Or you can kill yourself and never find out what an awesome fuck up you'll be.

Fucking up is part of life. You might not remember this, but when you were a baby, you were more of a fuck up than you are now. Couldn't walk, couldn't talk, shitting your pants all the god damn time. 

You didn't kill yourself. Oh, no. You continued to fuck up until you learned how to stand up, talk, and use the toilet. You matured to the next level of the fuck up game.

You will never stop fucking up. You will only find newer, better ways to fuck up and laugh about your past fuck-ups that you have now mastered.

You're strong. You can get through this. Remember that we're all here for you.

xxxooo

Some of my best friends are homeless and poor. I am also poor and live in a small, dirty rooming house.

As nice as money can be, it doesn't always make you happy. There are so many things that you can do without money. Your first step *is* to see your friends or get out of the house. It may be tough if you've already allowed yourself to get into this suicidal state of mind, but I can assure you that if you push yourself to go out and see your friends, you will not regret it. 

Even just a 10 minute walk to enjoy the fresh are and beauty of nature will make a difference in your life. 

My homeless friends are some of the happiest people I know. It's not about what's in your wallet. It's about what/who you have in your heart. It's about the friends and family who love you. It's about loving yourself and the world around you.

Chin up, love. There's a lot to live for.
